notes:
Lead: Head of Product (Ioana Marin) and Senior Eng Manager (Ben Chu). Mid-market SaaS focused on enterprise support teams. Primary eval is for an agent product that composes: canonical document search -> plan generation -> execute actions in customer CRM and calendar (multi-step agentic workflow).

Key requirements / ask: streaming responses for perceived latency (need streaming start <=300ms for short queries), deterministic tool-call semantics (idempotency, explicit ack), configurable tool-call timeouts (want 3s default, ability to raise to 10s per tool), and graceful fallback when tool call fails (rollback/no-op vs compensate). Concern: retries can cause duplicate writes in CRM - need at-least-once vs exactly-once guidance.

Performance targets discussed: median end-to-end (query -> first stream chunk) target ~200-300ms; 95th percentile tail <800ms for single-step flows. Throughput: baseline 50 concurrent agents (peaks to 150) with bursts; cost sensitivity — want guidance on batching/kv-cache for embeddings and generation to reduce token cost.

POC plan: 2-week hosted API POC using subset of production traffic with mock tooling endpoints (CRM sandbox + calendar). Tests to run: 1) streaming startup latency benchmarks, 2) tool-call reliability under network jitter (simulate 100-500ms added latency), 3) retry scenarios to validate duplicate suppression patterns, 4) model fallback when primary model is rate-limited. Metrics we will capture: first-byte time, per-token latency, tool-call latency distribution, failed action rate, and cost per completed session.

Client quotes/snippets: "We want agents that reliably complete multi-step tasks — not just good chat. If the tool fails midway, we need predictable behavior." — Ioana.

Legal / Security: SOC2 required; KMS preferred for production keys; data residency notes: US-only for now but European customers later. Asked about private deployment options and path to Dedicated with reserved capacity for predictable latency and budgets.

Internal notes: SE Miguel to prepare a short runbook for tool-call idempotency patterns (suggested approaches: idempotency keys, operation logs, compensating actions). AE Aisha to confirm POC pricing credit and provide clear path to Dedicated commit thresholds (QPS and committed spend).
use_case_summary: NexaAssist is evaluating Redwood Hosted API first to validate streaming + tool-calling reliability for an agentic workflow that searches internal docs and then performs actions in customer CRMs and calendars. If POC meets latency and reliability SLOs, they plan to transition to Dedicated for predictable throughput and cost containment.
short_description: Mid-market support automation vendor evaluating Redwood for agentic workflows (search + action). Hosted POC focused on streaming start latency and tool-call reliability; potential Dedicated later.
sales_notes: Pricing sensitivity: needs clear unit economics at 100k-500k monthly tokens. Wants an explicit migration path to Dedicated with commit thresholds. Ask: include burst capacity options in quote and show historical latency dashboards from similar customers.
technical_notes: Focus areas for SE: streaming SDK example, tool-call retry/ack patterns, sample idempotency patterns, synthetic harness to emulate network jitter, recommended quantization/model variants for 8-bit to lower cost without harming tool-calling reliability.
